projects.name: Project 1.2.1.4.1 Developing Juvenile justice in Libya II
projects.description:
Guided by the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and other relevant international and national legal frameworks, the Project builds on the achievements and lessons learned from the first Phase of this joint project “developing juvenile justice in Libya”.Building on the accomplishments of Phase I and informed by the recommendations and lessons learned identified during its final evaluation, Phase II of the project is designed to address emerging needs and leverage strategic opportunities for greater impact. This phase aims to support Libyan authorities in aligning the national legal framework with international laws, norms, and standards, while strengthening the juvenile justice system to ensure a more effective, child-centered approach.

Key priorities for Phase II include the institutionalization of child-friendly legal aid, the implementation of alternatives to detention, and the enhancement of detention conditions to better meet international standards. The project will also focus on raising awareness about children’s rights through targeted campaigns, establishing specialized procedures, and improving institutional capacities. Phase II seeks to contribute to a more peaceful, secure, and equitable society in Libya by fostering a rehabilitative and rights-based juvenile justice system.

Phase II effort directly supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Outcome 1.2: “By 2025, people in Libya participate in and benefit from a more peaceful, safe, and secure society, free from armed conflict and underpinned by unified and strengthened security, justice, rule of law, and human rights institutions.” Through this initiative, the project seeks to foster a more inclusive and protective environment for children in Libya, ensuring their rights are safeguarded and their development is nurtured.
projects.outcome: Non-discriminatory, enforceable, harmonized, and monitorable legal and policy frameworks are developed by legitimate authorities to promote rule of law in Libya in line with international human rights norms and standards.

projects.name: Project 1.2.1.4.1 Developing Juvenile justice in Libya II
projects.description:
Guided by the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and other relevant international and national legal frameworks, the Project builds on the achievements and lessons learned from the first Phase of this joint project “developing juvenile justice in Libya”.Building on the accomplishments of Phase I and informed by the recommendations and lessons learned identified during its final evaluation, Phase II of the project is designed to address emerging needs and leverage strategic opportunities for greater impact. This phase aims to support Libyan authorities in aligning the national legal framework with international laws, norms, and standards, while strengthening the juvenile justice system to ensure a more effective, child-centered approach.

Key priorities for Phase II include the institutionalization of child-friendly legal aid, the implementation of alternatives to detention, and the enhancement of detention conditions to better meet international standards. The project will also focus on raising awareness about children’s rights through targeted campaigns, establishing specialized procedures, and improving institutional capacities. Phase II seeks to contribute to a more peaceful, secure, and equitable society in Libya by fostering a rehabilitative and rights-based juvenile justice system.

Phase II effort directly supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Outcome 1.2: “By 2025, people in Libya participate in and benefit from a more peaceful, safe, and secure society, free from armed conflict and underpinned by unified and strengthened security, justice, rule of law, and human rights institutions.” Through this initiative, the project seeks to foster a more inclusive and protective environment for children in Libya, ensuring their rights are safeguarded and their development is nurtured.

projects.name: Project 1.1.1.8.4 Technical support and training of relevant actors (local and international) to address different needs of women and the WPS agenda in the humanitarian response
projects.description:
As part of UN Women’s ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional and individual capacities for inclusive humanitarian action, a three-day training on the Inclusive Humanitarian Action (GiHA) was successfully implemented from 23 to 25 June 2025 in Benghazi, in partnership with the local civil society organization Nuwasi. This activity contributes to enhancing technical expertise and operational readiness of local actors to address women’s specific needs and advance the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda within humanitarian response frameworks.

Building on the successful implementation of the initial Training of Trainers (ToT) conducted in December 2024 in Tripoli—delivered in partnership with the Libyan Red Crescent (LRC) and Ministry of Local Governance (MoLG)—this second training aimed to expand the geographic and institutional reach of capacity-building efforts. The June 2025 training targeted 19 participants, including local activists and frontline responders from Benghazi, Tobruk, Albayda, Shahhat, Slog, Magzaha, Kufra, and Derna. These participants represent a diverse cross-section of stakeholders directly engaged in community-based humanitarian response and local governance.

The training addressed two key outputs: (1) enhanced technical knowledge in core GiHA concepts, and (2) strengthened facilitation and training delivery skills. The curriculum was designed to ensure immediate applicability and included modules on foundational women empowerment principles, intersectional needs in crisis contexts, the use of Sex-Age-Disability Disaggregated Data (SADDD), and methodologies for gender analysis both before and after crises. Participants engaged in practical exercises to design and deliver community training modules focusing on women’s needs in crises, tailored to the specific needs of their areas.

The interactive training methodology fostered peer learning and participatory problem-solving, enabling participants to co-create solutions and adapt global good practices to the Libyan context. The inclusion of case studies from the MENA region, along with hands-on group assignments, reinforced knowledge retention and supported the development of context-relevant training.

This training activity, alongside the December 2024 ToT—which led to the cascading of training sessions reaching 184 additional community members—marks a sustained and scalable effort to institutionalize inclusive approaches within Libya’s humanitarian landscape. Both trainings contribute directly to the broader objective of operationalizing the WPS agenda through practical, locally led actions that ensure inclusive service delivery and community resilience during crises.

projects.name: Project 1.1.2.1.1 Policy analysis of existing institutional structures, legal framework that are enablers and/or act as potential barriers for women to take on decision making roles and positions, including dissemination of findings from research study among national counterparts to promote women in decision making positions.
projects.description:
A research titled “Libyan Women in Public Office and Decision-Making Positions”, was successfully published. The study applied a mixed-methods approach, incorporating qualitative interviews with 96 key administrative personnel from the Ministry of Local Governance and the Ministry of Planning. This methodological approach ensured the research was evidence-based, contextually relevant, and reflective of the current realities faced by women in Libya’s public sector and governance structures. As of July 2025, the study has recorded 102 pageviews by 67 unique users, with an average engagement time of 19 seconds per user. The platform registered 406 interactions (event count), and the report has been downloaded 28 times in Arabic and 19 times in English.
To support the dissemination of findings and promote national dialogue, UN Women Libya, in partnership with the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) and the Ministry of State for Women Affairs (MoWA), convened a national webinar on April 24th, 2025, coinciding with Libyan National Women’s Day. The webinar brought together 77 participants, including women’s rights advocates, civil society organizations, government representatives, and international partners.
During the event, MoWA expressed agreement with the study’s findings and demonstrated strong interest in leveraging the evidence to inform policy dialogue and future programming aimed at enhancing women’s representation in decision-making roles.
The event served as a platform to present the research findings, stimulate discussion around persistent barriers to women’s leadership, and share concrete recommendations to strengthen women’s participation in public office. The activity contributed to enhanced awareness among national stakeholders and positioned the research as an advocacy tool to support evidence-based policy reform promoting women in decision-making positions.

projects.name: Project 1.2.2.2.1 Capacity building for judges, prosecutors and law enforcement officials on EVAW, based on the findings and recommendations of the VAW study/analysis, towards the effective implementation of national frameworks
projects.description:
On June 27-28, 2025, UN Women Libya, in partnership with UNDP Libya and the organization “No Peace Without Justice” and in the context of the existing partnership between “the Human Rights, Transitional Justice and Rule of Law Division at UNSMIL”,  strengthened the capacities of Libyan CSOs active in the field of legal aid and built alliances and partnership between them by organizing the workshop “Legal Aid in the Libyan Context.”

 The workshop improved participants knowledge and strengthened their capacities  on international standards and guidelines of legal aid, important components of national legal aid systems, best practices regionally and internationally for providing legal aid, and initiatives of UN agencies in Libya operating in the field of legal aid through a participatory methodology, promoting open dialogue, experience-sharing, and joint problem-solving. Expert contributions provided a foundation for interactive sessions, during which participants explored legal aid challenges and formulated practical recommendations and initial proposals for developing an effective national legal aid framework throughout a comprehensive and human rights-based approach that applies to the need of the Libyan context.

As part of the workshop, UN Women presented key findings and recommendations from its study report "Protecting Libyan Women Lawyers from Violence," with a specific focus on the role of legal aid in responding to violence against women and girls (VAWG). This intervention highlighted the risks and challenges faced by Libyan women lawyers, particularly those providing legal aid in cases related to gender-based violence. The presentation emphasized the importance of integrating sensitive and survivor-centered approaches in national legal aid systems and contributed to discussions on policy and practical measures to better protect and support women legal professionals.

As a result of the workshop, 21 participants, including 6 Libyan women and 15 Libyan men, from CSOs active, experts interested in the field of legal aid in Libya improved their knowledge of legal aid practices and principles and strengthened their capacity toproviding legal aid through a comprehensive and human rights-based approach..

projects.name: Project 1.2.2.2.2 Provision of technical expertise to the Justice and Legal sector to design, budget, implement and monitor for inclusive access to justice in Libya, particularly for women
projects.description:
UN Women initiated the production of further technical expertise on inclusive access to justice in Libya by commissioning a report titled “Protecting Libyan Women Lawyers from Violence.” This report was prepared by two legal experts and represents a comprehensive effort to shed light on the violence faced by Women Lawyers in Libya. This data-based report analyses the legal and political frameworks related to Violence against Libyan Women Lawyers. It explores cultural, social, and institutional barriers that limit their role in the justice sector and and reinforce violent practices Additionally, the report examines the levels, types, and impacts of violence and the role of relevant stakeholders in mitigating this phenomenon. Through this comprehensive analysis, the report contributes valuable knowledge to the justice sector. 

 The study successfully engaged 76 Libyan Women Lawyers from different regions through  a comprehensive survey and focused group discussions  These data collection efforts provided critical insights into the nature of violence experience and the effectieness of existng support mechanisms.  Bases on the findings,  practical recommendations delivered to improve protection and prevent VAW Lawyers. These include proposing the development of legislative protections, capacity-building of judges, prosecutors, court staff, and security officials in the field of women’s rights and violence prevention, and the enhancement of the administrative complaint system to enable Women Lawyers to report incidents more effectively and easily. 

The report is currently being designed for publishing and then will be published. Publishing the report will proliferate the knowledge of technical frameworks and contribute to data that can acquire funding that can be utilized to enhance the protection of Women Lawyers. UN Women advanced the understanding and monitoring of violence faced by Women Lawyers in Libya and laid the groundwork for advocacy and capacity building of the Legal and Justice Sector by initiating this report.

UN Women further promoted inclusive access to justice in Libya by presenting the results and recommendations to the Rule of Law (RoL) meeting on July 7, 2025 to ___ attendees. The data was also presented at the “Legal Aid in the Libyan Context” workshop to twenty participants who are active in CSOs or interested in the field of legal aid in Libya.

A legal aid workshop is being organized for  the next quarter for participants who are active in CSOs or interested in the field of legal aid in Libya to increase their understanding of this topic and build on its intersection with the process of developing an effective national legal aid system.

projects.name: Assessment of the situation of internally displaced women and girls IDPs from Murzuq and Tawergha with a focus on durable solutions
projects.description:
UN Women implemented a results-oriented initiative aimed at strengthening inclusive durable solutions for conflict-affected populations in Murzuq and Tawergha, with a specific focus on displaced and returnee women. The initiative was designed to generate actionable evidence and enhance the leadership capacities of women from these communities, thereby contributing to more inclusive recovery and peacebuilding efforts.
A mixed-methods research study was successfully conducted in 2024 and finalized and published in 2025, to assess the needs, experiences, and aspirations of displaced and returnee women. The study engaged 289 women through structured surveys, 21 through focus group discussions, and 11 through key informant interviews. Led by a national researcher with field coordinators in both locations, the research also integrated feedback from women who had previously participated in UN Women’s capacity-building trainings. The report was professionally translated to Arabic and the two versions were then designed and printed and now available in hard copy and online. As of July 2025, the online version of the report has reached 181 page views by 117 unique users, with an average engagement time of 13 seconds per user. Interaction with the online platform (event count) reached 715, and the report has been downloaded 34 times in Arabic and 53 times in English. The evidence collected serves as a foundational input for women needs-sensitive planning and policy development in displacement contexts.
To ensure relevance and stakeholder ownership, a validation workshop was organized in January 2025, bringing together 38 (F 32 – M 6 ) representatives from civil society, UN agencies, and international organizations. Participants reviewed the findings and provided contextual insights to guide programmatic adjustments and promote alignment with ground realities.
Following the validation, UN Women finalized the report and proceeded with its production and dissemination. Despite security-related delays that led to the cancellation of the initially planned launch event on 26 February 2025 (which was cancelled after it had already begun the same day with 10 participants), UN Women successfully organized a second public dissemination event on 18 March 2025. The event, which included 25 participants ( 8 F – 7 M) from CSOs, NGOs, UN agencies, donors and other stakeholders via Zoom, served to amplify the voices of women affected by conflict and advocate for their inclusion in recovery and peacebuilding processes.
Complementing the research, UN Women conducted two capacity-building trainings to enhance the leadership, advocacy, and governance skills of women leaders from Murzuq, Tawergha, and surrounding displacement-affected communities. The first training in September 2024 engaged 20 participants, while the second in February 2025 reached 27 women leaders, including municipal councillors, civil society actors, academics, and government officials. Post-training feedback demonstrated strengthened confidence and competencies in community mobilization and inclusive governance.
Through this initiative, which included evidence generation, validation, production and dissemination, UN Women contributed to increasing the visibility of women’s priorities in conflict-affected areas, strengthened national capacity to address women needs, and fostered inclusive engagement around durable solutions in Libya.

projects.name: Project 1.2.1.4.1 Developing Juvenile justice in Libya II
projects.description:
Guided by the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and other relevant international and national legal frameworks, the Project builds on the achievements and lessons learned from the first Phase of this joint project “developing juvenile justice in Libya”.Building on the accomplishments of Phase I and informed by the recommendations and lessons learned identified during its final evaluation, Phase II of the project is designed to address emerging needs and leverage strategic opportunities for greater impact. This phase aims to support Libyan authorities in aligning the national legal framework with international laws, norms, and standards, while strengthening the juvenile justice system to ensure a more effective, child-centered approach.

Key priorities for Phase II include the institutionalization of child-friendly legal aid, the implementation of alternatives to detention, and the enhancement of detention conditions to better meet international standards. The project will also focus on raising awareness about children’s rights through targeted campaigns, establishing specialized procedures, and improving institutional capacities. Phase II seeks to contribute to a more peaceful, secure, and equitable society in Libya by fostering a rehabilitative and rights-based juvenile justice system.

Phase II effort directly supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Outcome 1.2: “By 2025, people in Libya participate in and benefit from a more peaceful, safe, and secure society, free from armed conflict and underpinned by unified and strengthened security, justice, rule of law, and human rights institutions.” Through this initiative, the project seeks to foster a more inclusive and protective environment for children in Libya, ensuring their rights are safeguarded and their development is nurtured.
